data.title: Cybersecurity is now a plant-floor discipline
data.excerpt: The control network is no longer isolated, and the maintenance laptop is part of the attack surface. Security has to be designed with operations, not handed to IT afterwards.
data.body:
Industrial security used to be a perimeter conversation: keep the plant network separate and assume the rest. Remote support, vendor access, and data projects have dissolved that assumption.

The practical risk is usually mundane: a compromised engineering laptop, an unpatched historian, or a shared password that turns a routine maintenance task into an outage.

Design for the maintenance reality

  • Inventory every remote access path, including vendor tools.

  • Separate engineering, operations, and enterprise zones with documented rules.

  • Use unique credentials and hardware-backed authentication for engineers.

  • Test restore procedures for historians and configuration backups.

Make security an operating routine

A secure architecture that nobody reviews decays. Assign ownership, schedule reviews after every significant change, and include security in commissioning acceptance. The plant team should be able to explain how to isolate a compromised asset without waiting for a corporate escalation.
